  3.  PUBLIC HEARING FOR AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND THE WESTLAKE
  VILLAGE MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO ACCESSORY DWELLING
  UNITS; ORDINANCE NO. 297-22

  Mayor Halpern opened the Public Hearing. Planning Director Forbes introduced
  Ordinance No. 297-22 to amend the Westlake Village Municipal Code pertaining
  to Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) development standards and application
  processing requirements. The amendments are required due to changes in State
  law effective January 1, 2023.

  On September 28, 2022, the Governor signed Assembly Bill 2221 and Senate Bill
  897. Both bills take effect January 1, 2023 and amend State law pertaining to
  ADUs. All cities are required to update their ADU standards to reflect the new
  legislation. The practical effect of the required changes will be minimal for
  Westlake Village, as described below.

  •  Height: There are no properties in Westlake Village within one-half mile of
  a major transit stop or high-quality transit corridor, so the height increase
  for detached ADUs will not be applicable. The City's existing ADU standards
  already allow attached ADUs of the same height allowed for the primary
  residence, so the required change would only apply in situations where
  someone desired to build a two-story ADU attached to a single-story
  primary dwelling. This scenario is not allowed under the current standards
  but would be allowed under the new State-mandated standards. However,
  the attached two-story ADU would be limited to 25 feet in height. Detached
  ADUs would still be limited to 16 feet.

  •  Front setback: Most or all properties in the City have adequate space in
  rear or side yard areas to accommodate an ADU, which makes it
  unnecessary to encroach into the front yard setback.

  •  Junior ADUs: While an attached garage may now be converted into a
  Junior ADU, the same space could be converted into an attached ADU
  under current standards, so this change is minor.

  •  Processing: The required changes to how an application is processed are
  entirely procedural and have no practical effect on the approval or
  construction of an ADU, or on the City's ability to regulate ADU construction
  and enforce other applicable requirements.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  November 9, 2022  10
PUBLIC HEARINGS (continued):

  Ordinances implementing State ADU law are exempt from environmental review
  under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section
  15282(h) of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  On November 2, 2022, the Land Use Committee (Pearl/Honig) recommended that
  the request be moved forward to the full City Council for a public hearing.

  Mayor Halpern closed the Public Hearing.

Mayor Pro Tern Pearl moved that Ordinance No. 297-22, 'An Ordinance of the City of
Westlake Village Regarding Accessory Dwelling Unit and Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit
Regulations, Amending the Westlake Village Municipal Code,' be introduced by title only
and that further reading be waived with a second reading on December 14, 2022 and
determining that adopting this Accessory Dwelling Unit Ordinance is exempt from CEQA
pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15282(h). Councilmember Honig seconded the
motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Mcsweeney, Honig, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl, and

  BUILDING. ELECTRICAL, PLUMBING, MECHANICAL. RESIDENTIAL GREEN
  BUILDING STANDARDS. AND EXISTING BUILDING CODES: AND THE 2022
  CALIFORNIA FIRE CODE: TOGETHER WITH CERTAIN AMENDMENTS,
  DELETIONS, AND ADDITIONS; AND INCLUDING FINDINGS, FEES. AND
  PENALTIES; ORDINANCE NO. 298-22

  Planning Director Forbes introduced Ordinance No. 298-22, to adopt by reference
  the 2022 editions of the Los Angeles County Building, Electrical, Plumbing,
  Mechanical, Residential, Green Building Standards, and Existing Building Codes,
  and the 2022 California Fire Code. Without City Council action, the California
  Building Standards Code will automatically become effective on January 1, 2023,
  without the benefit of local amendments.

  Every three years, the California Building Standards Commission adopts a new
  version of the California Building Standards Code, codified in Title 24 of the
  California Code of Regulations. The California Building Standards Code governs
  the construction of all structures in the state and consists of the California Building,
  Residential, Electrical, Mechanical, Plumbing, Energy, Historical Building, Fire,
  Existing Building, Green Building Standards, and Referenced Standards Codes.
  With each triennial update of the California Building Standards Code, Los Angeles
  County adopts by reference the updated code along with local amendments.
  These amendments are developed with consideration for the County's unique
  climatic, geologic, and topographic conditions.

  The proposed ordinance adopts by reference all the County codes referenced
  except the Fire Code. The County is still in the process of drafting local
  amendments to the 2022 edition of the California Fire Code. Once the County has

  PAINTING PROJECT, PHASE 2

  City Engineer Hughes presented the results of the solicitation for bids and
  requested City Council approval to award a construction agreement to Streetlight
  Restoration Specialists in the amount of $186,000 for the implementation of Phase
  2 of the Traffic Signal Painting Project.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  November 9, 2022  14
NEW BUSINESS (continued):

  The bid opening was held on October 27, 2022, where the City received one bid
  for the project. This bid is 3% below the engineer's estimate of $192,000. The
  total bid amount includes all three additive alternates. Although only one bid was
  received, readvertising the project likely would not result in additional bids and
  would therefore not be in the City's best interest.

  The Traffic Signal Painting Project, Phase 2 is exempt from California
  Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA") review pursuant to the Class 1 categorical
  exemption of the State CEQA Guidelines (14 C.C.R. § 15301). Among other
  things, that exemption applies to maintenance of existing facilities involving no
  expansion of use. The project also is exempt as an activity having no potential for
  causing a significant effect on the environment (14 C.C.R. § 15061 (b)(3)).

  Mayor Pro Tern Pearl moved to determine the Traffic Signal Painting Project,
  Phase 2 is exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Sections 15301 and
  15061 (b)(3), award a construction contract for the Traffic Signal Painting Project,
  Phase 2, consisting of the base bid items plus all three additive alternates, to
  Streetlight Restoration Specialists in the amount of $186,000 with construction
  contingency of $9,300; and authorize the Mayor to execute the construction
  contract on behalf of the City. Councilmember Mcsweeney seconded the motion.
